 Asset Description : 
 A Tier 4 diesel engine with Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) is a type of industrial engine that meets the stringent emissions standards set by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). The engine is equipped with an SCR system, which uses a liquid reductant, such as diesel exhaust fluid (DEF), to reduce harmful nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions. The main components of a Tier 4 diesel engine with SCR include the engine block, cylinder head, piston, connecting rod, crankshaft, camshaft, fuel system, cooling system, exhaust system, and the SCR system.

The engine block is the main structure of the engine and contains the cylinders, where the pistons move up and down. The cylinder head sits on top of the engine block and contains the valves and spark plugs. The piston is moved up and down by the connecting rod, which is connected to the crankshaft. The crankshaft converts the linear motion of the piston into rotational motion. The camshaft controls the opening and closing of the valves, which allow air and fuel to enter the cylinder and exhaust gases to exit. The fuel system delivers fuel to the engine and the cooling system removes excess heat. The exhaust system removes exhaust gases from the engine and the SCR system treats the exhaust gases to reduce NOx emissions.

The SCR system typically includes a catalyst, a dosing module, and a DEF tank. The catalyst is a device that promotes a chemical reaction between the exhaust gases and the reductant, and the dosing module injects the reductant into the exhaust stream. The DEF tank stores the reductant. The SCR system also includes sensors and a control unit to monitor and control the SCR process. The sensors measure the temperature, pressure, and composition of the exhaust gases and the reductant, and the control unit adjusts the amount of reductant injected and the timing of the injection to optimize the SCR process. Additionally, the engine may also be equipped with a diesel particulate filter (DPF) to reduce particulate matter emissions. The DPF captures and burns off particulate matter from the exhaust gases.

It is important to note that the maintenance of Tier 4 diesel engine with SCR is crucial to ensure its optimal performance and longevity. Regular inspections, fluid changes, and filter replacements are some of the key maintenance tasks that should be performed on a regular basis. Additionally, the DEF tank should be filled regularly and the level of the reductant should be monitored to ensure that the SCR system is functioning properly.
